Q2.answer:
(a) Wine $40,000, 50% rate = $20,000 when duty applies. Entry 1 Aug. 20, 2:00 p.m.: $0. Entry 2 Aug. 21, 11:59 p.m.: $0. Entry 3 Aug. 22, 12:01 a.m.: $40,000×50%=$20,000.
(b) Proc. 11046 itself prints Aug. 19 in para.9, clause (1) and clause (3), 91 FR 46640-46641. Suspension Proc. 11056 clause (1), 91 FR 54790, provides the effective date shall be Aug. 22 and amends only the chapeau of Annex II of each original proclamation (deleting Aug. 19, inserting Aug. 22). Clauses (1)/(3) of the originals were not textually amended. The later operative effective-date direction, plus suspension clause (5) superseding inconsistent previous provisions, resolves the difference in favour of Aug. 22; later recitals (e.g. 11061 para.4) confirm duties became effective Aug. 22.
(c) Documents say refunds, if implementation requires them, are processed under applicable law and CBP standard procedures, Proc. 11056 clause (4), 91 FR 54791, and agencies shall as soon as practicable suspend collection, clause (2). No automatic or interest-bearing refund mechanism is stated in the readable text. Entry 1 was before the Aug. 22 effective date, so the deposit was not legally owed.
(d) No further presidential action was needed to begin: the original proclamation imposed the duty effective Aug. 19, clause (1), and the suspension merely postponed that date to Aug. 22. Later documents say Canada reneged Aug. 21, the 3-day suspension lapsed at 12:01 a.m. Aug. 22, and duties became effective then, e.g. Proc. 11061 paras.3-4, 91 FR 58311.
(e) §338 as recited in Proc. 11046 para.10, 91 FR 46640: duties may not take effect earlier than 30 days after the finding proclamation. Finding/signed July 20, 2026 + 30 days = Aug. 19, 2026 (July 20→July 31 = 11 days, +19 days in August = 30).

Q3.answer:
(a) Beer $30,000, MFN free, §338 50%×$30,000=$15,000 when duty applies.
A. Arrives Sept. 10, entered Sept. 14: may be imported; §338 $15,000. Ban applies only to goods imported on/after Sept. 29.
B. Arrives Sept. 27, warehouse, withdrawn Oct. 5: may be imported (imported before Sept. 29); §338 $15,000 on withdrawal, per exclusion clause (2) (imported but not entered/withdrawn before Sept. 29 remains subject to 50%).
C. Arrives 11:30 p.m. Sept. 28, entry filed 9:00 a.m. Sept. 29: may be imported (imported before 12:01 a.m. Sept. 29); §338 $15,000. Ban is measured by importation, not entry filing.
D. Arrives 12:30 a.m. Sept. 29: may not be imported — excluded from importation for goods imported on/after 12:01 a.m. Sept. 29. No consumption entry that morning; no §338 duty is owed on a shipment that is not imported.
(b) Shipment E arrives/admitted to FTZ Sept. 25, entry Oct. 6: imported before ban, so not banned. FTZ admission on/after the §338 effective date (Aug. 22) must be as privileged foreign status (unless domestic-status eligible), and duty applies on entry for consumption: $15,000.
(c) If the ban is held invalid as applied, clause (9)(b) provides the 50% duty in Proc. 11046 applies to the import to which the invalidated ban applied before invalidation. Post-ruling shipments that would have been banned therefore bear $15,000 per $30,000 shipment under clause (9)(b), 91 FR 58313.
(d) No. Exclusion clause (3) provides that besides changing Annex products from duty to ban, it does not otherwise affect products subject to the duty as established in the scope proclamation. Non-Annex listed products remain subject to 50% (subject to scope/§232 rules).
Q3.basis: Exclusion Proc. 11061 clause (1) imported on/after Sept. 29, clause (2) imported-but-not-entered products remain at 50%, clause (3) no other effect, clause (9)(b) severability duty, 91 FR 58312-58313. Original FTZ clause (4), 91 FR 46641. Scope proc. not touching this beer per scenario.

Q11.answer:
1. §338 start date: Original operative text says Aug. 19 — Proc. 11046 para.9, clause (1), clause (3), 91 FR 46640-46641; same in 11047/11048. Later recitals repeat Aug. 19 — e.g. Proc. 11061 para.1, 91 FR 58311; Proc. 11064 para.1, 91 FR 58331. But 11061 para.4, 91 FR 58311, and every later recital para.4, say duties became effective Aug. 22 at 12:01 a.m. Operative suspension clause (1) makes Aug. 22 the effective date.
2. Suspension described as 3 days vs. date change: Proc. 11056 paras.4-5, 91 FR 54790, say suspending for a period of 3 days; operative clause (1), 91 FR 54790, does not impose a 3-day suspension that then expires by its own terms — it deletes Aug. 19 and inserts Aug. 22 in the Annex II chapeaus, and later documents treat Aug. 22 as the (indefinite) commencement date. Clause (2) also directs suspending collection, although on Aug. 18 collection had not yet begun under the Aug. 19 date.
3. Dairy scope proclamation that does not exist: Proc. 11062 clause (3), 91 FR 58320, says the exclusion does not otherwise affect products as established in the Sept. 8, 2026 dairy scope-modification proclamation. No dairy scope proclamation was published in the series (only alcohol 11064 and motor 11065, 91 FR 58331, 58339). Alcohol/motor exclusions correctly cite their scope proclamations.
4. §301 proposal category misdescribed: Memo recital, 91 FR 47719, describes the proposed 10% group as economies that impose a ban but do not yet effectively enforce it (Canada, Ecuador, EU, Indonesia, Mexico, Pakistan). June proposal §III-IV, 91 FR 34274, lists those six as having failed to effectively enforce (not failed to impose) and proposes 10% for economies that impose a ban. USTR notice summary, 91 FR 47318, likewise says proposed 10% was for economies that impose a ban/ART/partial regime, omitting the memo's formulation.
5. All-failed-both vs. lists: USTR notice §I, 91 FR 47318, lists 54 economies that failed to impose and effectively enforce and six that failed to effectively enforce, then states all have failed to impose and to effectively enforce (failed both). June proposal, 91 FR 34274, contains the same concluding sentence. The six-economy list is inconsistent with the all-failed-both conclusion.
6. Textile mechanism rate in proposal: Memo recital, 91 FR 47719, says USTR proposed a textile mechanism allowing imports at a zero §301 rate. June proposal §IV, 91 FR 34274, says the proposal would allow textile/apparel imports at a reduced §301 rate (volume tied to U.S. textile/cotton exports). Adopted TRQs are free of §301 duty, Memo §2, 91 FR 47721.
7. §301 summary conflates net-rate economies: USTR notice SUMMARY, 91 FR 47318, describes 10% for ban/ART/partial economies with specific economies at 10% net, implying net treatment is within the 10% group. Operative Memo §1(a)(ii), 91 FR 47720, and §II.B, 91 FR 47323-47327, impose 12.5% net for Japan, Korea and Switzerland — outside the 10% group.
8. TRQ timing: Memo recital, 91 FR 47720, says TRQs will be feasible by Sept. 1, 2026. Operative Memo §2(a),(b), 91 FR 47721, directs establishment as soon as USTR determines it is feasible, with no Sept. 1 deadline.
9. §301 FTZ wording vs. §338 FTZ wording is not a discrepancy in rate, but in USTR notice §II.A, 91 FR 47321, FTZ privileged-foreign-status is effective as of the date the duty is imposed, whereas §338 original clause (4), 91 FR 46641, applies to FTZ admissions on/after the effective date; the §301 DATES line, 91 FR 47318, gives July 24 while Annex I.B, 91 FR 47394, later (July 31) adds the patented-pharmaceutical exemption without the DATES line disclosing it. These are noted as descriptive gaps, not operative conflicts, and are listed once here.
10. Scope-proclamation waiting period: Scope recitals, e.g. Proc. 11064 para.8, 91 FR 58332; Proc. 11076 para.9, 91 FR 68862, recite §338 duties may not take effect earlier than 30 days after the finding proclamation, yet operative scope clauses apply 7 days after signing (Sept. 8→Sept. 15; Oct. 23→Oct. 30). The scope documents do not explain the fit; they rely on the same paragraph's authority to suspend/revoke/supplement/amend.
Q11.basis: Citations in each numbered item above, with operative clauses distinguished from recitals/preamble. Drafting checked against Memo §§1-2, 91 FR 47720-47721; USTR notice §§I-II, 91 FR 47318-47321; June proposal §§III-IV, 91 FR 34274; §338 procs. 11046-11076 as cited.
Q11.uncertainty: Matters on which documents are silent or that appear only in image annexes are not listed as discrepancies, per instructions. Item 9 is a textual difference in timing language, not a rate conflict.

Q13.answer:
§232 duty only. Machine $200,000, Annex I-C, most metal smelted/melted outside U.S., no onshoring plan. June Proc. 11032 clause (2) applies June 8, 2026-Dec. 31, 2027, 91 FR 34087.
(a) Canada USMCA, U.S. parts $60,000: non-U.S. content $200,000−$60,000=$140,000; 25%×$140,000=$35,000. Effective 17.5%, above 15% floor, so $35,000.
(b) No U.S. content: $200,000×25%=$50,000.
(c) Canada non-USMCA: clause (2)(d) USMCA carve-out does not apply; clause (2)(a) 25% on full value (Apr. Proc. 11021 clause (1), full value) = $200,000×25%=$50,000.
(d) Japan, MFN 2.5%: Japan is listed in clause (2)(b); MFN 2.5%<15%, so §232 = (15%−2.5%)=12.5%×$200,000=$25,000. MFN duty $5,000 not counted in §232 amount asked.
(e) U.S. parts $20,000 + $30,000 U.S.-smelted aluminum in Canadian part: non-U.S. content is total minus parts produced in U.S. = $200,000−$20,000=$180,000 (the $30,000 is not a U.S.-produced part). Clause (2)(c) 10% net does not apply: most metal is outside U.S., so the 85%-by-weight deemed-entirely-U.S. rule, clause (4), 91 FR 34088, fails. $180,000×25%=$45,000 (22.5%, above floor).
(f) Oct. 6, 2026: same as (e), $45,000. No readable change between Oct. 6 and Oct. 20; June clause (2) runs to Dec. 31, 2027 and July Proc. 11045 is only an onshoring incentive, inapplicable here.
(g) U.S. parts $140,000: non-U.S. $60,000×25%=$15,000, effective 7.5%, below 15% floor. Floor raises duty to 15%×$200,000=$30,000.
(h) (a) treatment applies until 11:59 p.m. EST Dec. 31, 2027, June clause (2). From Jan. 1, 2028, clause (3)(a) applies the rates in Apr. Proc. 11021 clause (3) (Annex I-B rates, 25% unless lower), 91 FR 34088 — i.e. 25% on full value, $50,000, with no USMCA non-U.S.-content carve-out in the readable text.

Q14.answer:
1. Partly correct. Memo recital, 91 FR 47720, says TRQs are not feasible now but will be feasible by Sept. 1, 2026. Operative §2, 91 FR 47721, says as soon as USTR determines it is feasible — no Sept. 1 deadline.
2. Incorrect for the June proposal. Over 450 comments/nearly 60 witnesses describes the March initiation round, June proposal §I, 91 FR 34273. For the June proposal, USTR received over 1,600 written comments and over 100 witnesses, Memo, 91 FR 47719; USTR notice §I, 91 FR 47319.
3. Partly correct. Seven economies moved to 10%: six adopted bans (Cambodia, Guatemala, Honduras, India, Sri Lanka, Trinidad and Tobago) and Jordan undertook an ART commitment, Memo, 91 FR 47720; USTR notice §I, 91 FR 47319. Not each adopted a ban.
4. Incorrect. Commenters suggested removing beef/avocados (and paprika, lithium hexafluorophosphate, forgings) linking them to forced labor, USTR notice §III.C.3, 91 FR 47331. USTR determined not to remove these products.
5. Incorrect. Net-of-MFN economies are EU, Taiwan, Japan, Korea, Switzerland, Memo §1(a)(ii), 91 FR 47720. EU (Part C), Taiwan (Part K) and Switzerland (Part D) have economy-specific Annex II parts, but Japan and Korea are excepted only by Annex I and Annex II Part A, §§II.B.28, 49, 91 FR 47324, 47327 — no own negotiated list.
6. Partly correct. USTR excluded an additional 471 products in each investigation, §III.D, 91 FR 47331, and exempted certain sugar and sugar-containing products, §§III.D, 91 FR 47331-47333 — not all sugar products.
7. Incorrect. Only net-rate economies are capped so MFN+§301 =10% or 12.5%, §§II.B.19, 28, 51, 52, 91 FR 47323-47327. Flat-rate economies pay §301 in addition to MFN, Note 52(a), 91 FR 47352 (e.g. MFN 4% +12.5% =16.5%).
8. Correct. USTR notice §II.A, 91 FR 47321: FTZ-admitted products subject to the duty, except domestic-status-eligible, only may be admitted as privileged foreign status, effective as of the date the duty is imposed.
9. Correct. Memo §4(e), 91 FR 47723; USTR notice §IV, 91 FR 47335: if an exemption is held invalid, the applicable tariff applies to imports to which the invalidated exemption applied before invalidation.
10. Correct. USTR notice §III.C, 91 FR 47330: exempt all Annex A proposed products except non-pharmaceutical applications of certain chemicals; determined not to remove additional products.
